sacred.note: Traditional reckoning as stated in the cited texts; it is not a historical or scientific chronology and is not drawn on the same axis as scholarly dates.

sacred.name: Junction of Dvāpara and Kali (Kṛṣṇa and the Kurukṣetra war)
sacred.description: Traditional chronology: the Nārāyaṇīya foretells Kṛṣṇa's birth at Mathurā 'at the final junction of Dvāpara and Kali' (MBh CE 12.326.82); the Kurukṣetra war and the Yādava destruction belong to this junction in tradition, and Kali begins on the day Kṛṣṇa leaves the earth (ViP 4.24.27, 4.24.32; 5.38.8).

sources.quote: dvāparasya kaleś caiva saṃdhau paryavasānike / prādurbhāvaḥ kaṃsahetor mathurāyāṃ bhaviṣyati

sources.edition: Critical edition, M. M. Pathak (Vadodara 1997–99); GRETIL e-text by P. Schreiner

sacred.note: Tradition equates this junction with the Kali epoch of 3102 BCE (see sac:kali-yuga). Traditional reckoning as stated in the cited texts; it is not a historical or scientific chronology and is not drawn on the same axis as scholarly dates.

sacred.name: Kali yuga (current)
sacred.description: Traditional chronology: the fourth and present age: 1,000 divine years with junctions of 100 each = 1,200 (432,000 human years at 360:1); ViP 4.24.33 gives 360,000 human years and 4.24.34 '1,200 divine years'. It begins when Kṛṣṇa departs (ViP 4.24.32; 5.38.8). Indian astronomy from Āryabhaṭa (499 CE: Kali 3600 in his 23rd year, AB 3.10) fixes its epoch at 3102 BCE, and the Aihole inscription of 634/635 CE counts 3,735 years since the Bhārata war.

sources.edition: GRETIL e-text, text of Kullūka (Shastri 1983) with Medhātithi variants
Critical edition, M. M. Pathak (Vadodara 1997–99); GRETIL e-text by P. Schreiner
sources.quote: trīṇi lakṣāṇi varṣāṇāṃ dvija mānuṣasaṃkhyayā / ṣaṣṭiṃ caiva sahasrāṇi bhaviṣyaty eṣa vai kaliḥ

sacred.note: The 3102 BCE epoch is an astronomical-traditional computation (Fleet 1911; Pingree 1981); it is not evidence for the date of any narrated event. The 360,000 of ViP 4.24.33 is recorded as the e-text reads. Traditional reckoning as stated in the cited texts; it is not a historical or scientific chronology and is not drawn on the same axis as scholarly dates.

sacred.name: End of Kali and advent of Kalki
sacred.description: Traditional chronology: at the junction closing the Kali age Kalki is born at Śambhala to Viṣṇuyaśas and restores the Kṛta age (BhP 1.3.25, 12.2.16–20; MatsP 47.247–251; AgP 16.7–10).

sources.quote: athāsau yugasandhyāyāṃ dasyuprāyeṣu rājasu / janitā viṣṇuyaśaso nāmnā kalkir jagatpatiḥ

sources.edition: Calcutta: Caukhamba Vidyabhavan 1954; GRETIL e-text (O. Hellwig), adhy. 1–176
Rajendralal Mitra ed. (Bibliotheca Indica 1870–79); GRETIL e-text

sacred.note: Traditional reckoning as stated in the cited texts; it is not a historical or scientific chronology and is not drawn on the same axis as scholarly dates.

sacred.name: Āryabhaṭa's mahāyuga of equal quarters (alternative system)
sacred.description: Traditional chronology: in the Āryabhaṭīya a mahāyuga of 12,000 divine years (4,320,000 years) is divided into four equal yugapādas of 1,080,000 years, unlike the 4:3:2:1 Purāṇic proportions; a divine year is 360 solar years (AB 3.7–8).
sacred.note: An astronomical reworking of the traditional scheme. Traditional reckoning as stated in the cited texts; it is not a historical or scientific chronology and is not drawn on the same axis as scholarly dates.

sacred.name: Night of Brahmā (naimittika pralaya)
sacred.description: Traditional chronology: at the end of each day of Brahmā the three worlds are burned and flooded; Brahmā-Nārāyaṇa sleeps on the serpent for a night as long as the day (ViP 1.3.22–25; Manu 1.72–73; BhP 12.7.17).

sources.edition: Critical edition, M. M. Pathak (Vadodara 1997–99); GRETIL e-text by P. Schreiner
GRETIL e-text, text of Kullūka (Shastri 1983) with Medhātithi variants

sacred.note: The Devī Māhātmya's Madhu–Kaiṭabha episode is set during Viṣṇu's cosmic sleep. Traditional reckoning as stated in the cited texts; it is not a historical or scientific chronology and is not drawn on the same axis as scholarly dates.
